answer:
**FINAL HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded):**

The variable is **SES — the respondent's family socioeconomic status** (the `SES` composite). In the social-background baseline model its effect on BA degree completion is strongly positive and significant; once **race (Black, Hispanic) and academic characteristics (ASVAB test-score composite + high-school class percentile)** are added, the SES effect **collapses by ~66%–109%, flips sign to negative, and loses significance** — the quoted trajectory (0.3636 → −0.2293, becoming insignificant) is the SES effect being absorbed/mediated by academic resources (and race). No other variable (family size, Male, race, ability, percentile) exhibits this positive-significant → negative/insignificant trajectory; family size stays negative and significant, and Male is never significant regardless of controls.

**What I actually reproduced (vs. the two quoted numbers) — transparent:**

| Model (SES coefficient) | M1 baseline (SES+Famsize+Male) | M4 full (+Black +Hispanic +Ability +Pctile) | Attenuation | Significance @ α=.05 in full |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **OLS / linear-prob.** (robust HC3) | **+0.0142** (p<0.001) | **−0.0013** (p=0.661) | −109% (sign flip) | **INSIGNIFICANT** |
| Logit | +0.8444 (p<0.001) | +0.2906 (p=0.010) | −66% | significant (marginal) |
| Probit | **+0.3662** (p<0.001) | +0.1263 (p=0.015) | −66% | significant (marginal) |

- **0.3636 → recovered almost exactly by the probit baseline:** SES = **+0.3662** (within 0.003) with the social-control baseline.
- **−0.2293 → recovered almost exactly by the logistic full model when the baseline is SES-only** (full = SES + Black + Hispanic + Ability + Pctile): SES = **+0.4729 → −0.2316** (p=0.021), within 0.002 of −0.2293. Ability-only academic set gives +0.4729 → −0.2413.
- **No single family+spec reproduces BOTH quotes in one run.** Closest single pair overall = Logit/SES-only baseline: d²=0.0120, error driven almost entirely by the baseline (0.4729 vs 0.3636), the full value being essentially on target (−0.2316 vs −0.2293). Standardized (beta) OLS also flips sign: +0.0612 → −0.0290 (p=0.017). Conclusion: the two quoted numbers straddle model details (family choice/control set) that this processed file cannot pin down exactly, but both endpoints are each matched to within ~0.003 by a natural SES specification, and the qualitative story (positive-significant → attenuated/negative/insignificant when race+academics added) holds across OLS, logit, probit, raw and standardized.
- **"Becoming insignificant"** is reproduced only in the linear-probability (OLS) model (p=0.66); logit (p=0.010) and probit (p=0.015) leave SES marginally significant — so the quote's "insignificant" wording corresponds to the LPM/OLS reading.

**Block-regression table (all 3 families, coefficient (p-value)):**

OLS: SES 0.0142(.000)→0.0138(.000;+race)→−0.0020(.470;+acad)→−0.0013(.661;both). Famsize always ≈−0.008/−0.010 (p<0.001). Male ≈−0.003/−0.006 (p≈0.08–0.34). Ability ~+0.0001, Pctile ~+0.0005 (both p<0.001).
Logit: SES 0.8444→0.8196→0.2695→0.2906. Famsize −0.61→−0.52 (p<0.001). Male −0.25→−0.27 (p≈0.07). Black −0.30→+0.52(p=.023). Ability +0.0025, Pctile +0.0234.
Probit: SES 0.3662→0.3566→0.1144→0.1263. Famsize −0.25→−0.21. Male −0.11→−0.12 (p≈0.06–0.12). Black −0.11→+0.26(p=.010). Ability +0.0011, Pctile +0.0106.

**Corroborating mediation evidence:** SES correlates +0.46 with Ability and +0.30 with class percentile; BA completion rises with SES tercile (low 1.6% → mid 2.9% → high 3.5%); these academic resources are strongly predictive of BA completion and are exactly what "academic characteristics" measure (test-score composite and class standing are the standard way to gauge academic performance in this data).

payload.hypothesis: SES (family socioeconomic status): its positive effect on BA degree completion (baseline ~0.36, probit) attenuates by ~66-109%, flips sign to negative (down to ~-0.2293) and becomes insignificant once race (Black, Hispanic) and academic characteristics (ASVAB test-score composite, class percentile) are added to the model.
payload.workflow: Hierarchical block regression (M1 social background -> M2 +race -> M3 +academic characteristics -> M4 +both) across linear-probability OLS (HC3), logit, and probit; standardized/beta and bivariate-baseline robustness sweeps to recover the quoted 0.3636/-0.2293 pair; SES identified as the only variable with a positive-significant baseline that collapses/sign-flips/becomes insignificant when race + academic characteristics are added.
